partners.mechanism_chain: GP6 (HGNC:4377) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0007599); Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0007599) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0001871); PROS1 (HGNC:9998) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —DECREASES→ Activated Protein C (APC) (CHEBI:17791); Activated Protein C (APC) (CHEBI:17791) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0002177). Mutations in GP6 impair platelet activation and aggregation, leading to bleeding. Mutations in PROS1 impair the function of Protein S, a cofactor for Activated Protein C (APC), leading to a hypercoagulable state and thrombophilia. Both diseases converge on the dysregulation of hemostasis, though through different arms of the coagulation system.

partners.mechanism_chain: IGLL1 (HGNC:5484) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050714); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050714) —LEADS_TO→ Severe B cell deficiency (HP:0003231); GP6 (HGNC:4570) —BINDS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050714); GP6 (HGNC:4570) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001894). Loss of function in IGLL1 (Disease B) directly impairs the B cell receptor signaling pathway, leading to severe B cell deficiency. GP6 (Disease A), while not directly involved in B cell development, has been shown to interact with components of the B cell receptor signaling pathway and its disruption can lead to thrombocytopenia. Therefore, mutations in IGLL1 disrupt the B cell receptor signaling pathway, leading to severe B cell deficiency. GP6 interacts with this pathway and its disruption leads to thrombocytopenia, thus both diseases converge on the B cell receptor signaling pathway.

#### 1. thrombophilia due to protein S deficiency, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.408)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-202733)

**Proposed mechanism:** GP6 (HGNC:4377) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0007599); Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0007599) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0001871); PROS1 (HGNC:9998) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —DECREASES→ Activated Protein C (APC) (CHEBI:17791); Activated Protein C (APC) (CHEBI:17791) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0002177). Mutations in GP6 impair platelet activation and aggregation, leading to bleeding. Mutations in PROS1 impair the function of Protein S, a cofactor for Activated Protein C (APC), leading to a hypercoagulable state and thrombophilia. Both diseases converge on the dysregulation of hemostasis, though through different arms of the coagulation system.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that GP6 variants do not affect platelet function or that PROS1 variants do not impact coagulation factor activity. _(variant: rs121918406 (GP6 c.1162G>A, p.Gly388Ser) with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the interplay between platelet function and coagulation can inform the development of novel therapeutic strategies for bleeding disorders and thrombotic conditions, potentially targeting shared regulatory pathways.

GP6 (Disease A), while not directly involved in B cell development, has been shown to interact with components of the B cell receptor signaling pathway and its disruption can lead to thrombocytopenia. Therefore, mutations in IGLL1 disrupt the B cell receptor signaling pathway, leading to severe B cell deficiency. GP6 interacts with this pathway and its disruption leads to thrombocytopenia, thus both diseases converge on the B cell receptor signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in IGLL1 that do not lead to loss-of-function, or evidence that GP6 does not interact with the B cell signaling pathway in a manner that could lead to immune dysregulation. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link via the B cell receptor signaling pathway could reveal novel therapeutic targets for immune dysregulation in both diseases, potentially involving modulation of B cell receptor signaling or related immune checkpoints.
